rationale: Both independently converge on the two hardest ground-truth bugs (stream-slot leak via id-space mismatch, and v2 codec being tried first for legacy checkpoints sharing model_type), plus several shared secondary findings (NPU dummy-run seq_token_counts gap, dead _finish_empty_streaming_requests code, talker_mtp hardcoded sampling params, WER PCM fallback) — strong evidence both are grounded rather than fabricated. Y edges ahead on recall/precision: its root-cause for the slot leak (the async_chunk/num_scheduled_tokens gating that prevents on_requests_finished from firing) matches the ground-truth reviewer's own reasoning almost verbatim, it catches the vendored-provenance-header note the ground truth also raised, and it surfaces one more genuine major bug (seq_token_counts sum-equality vs. padded token count) that X misses; its claims are also grep-verified rather than asserted. X is more actionable as a human-readable artifact (clean Blocking/Should-fix/Minor structure vs. Y's dense evidence-dump formatting with leaking list syntax) and finds its own unique valid issues (Realtime yaml slot capacity, KV-cache pre-profiling allocation), but includes one speculative/unverifiable claim (asserting CI is red). Neither candidate catches the two ground-truth Medium findings (cumulative-to-delta chunk_np re-slice bug, or the ceil-division/padding bug in audio_tokenizer_v2.py:949).
